correctness.rationale: All 5,887 nonempty simplices reconstructed from a standalone explicit edge list, the canonical graph-distance antipode checked, and exact rank tables in the plus and minus eigenspace chain complexes computed modulo 3 and 5. Independent unsplit boundary ranks agree with sums. UCT plus absence of H_5 mod 3 and H_4 mod 5 identify the nonzero 3-primary subgroup of H_3 and its minus sign. Exactness of two-group invariants away from characteristic two gives the stated quotient homology. Finite code is included and replayed; no infinite-computation claim.

value.rationale: The three-torsion in a canonical planar graph matching complex is already a motivated counterexample to a planar sphere-wedge conjecture. Determining whether its central geometric symmetry preserves or annihilates that torsion on quotient is a natural nonformal question. The minus action and 40-dimensional torsion-free three-local quotient describe behavior invisible from the known nonequivariant Betti numbers and abstract homotopy decomposition; this is not an arbitrary numerical slice.
